title: Opening a Real Port: The Twenty Lines That Decide Everything
fallback: No hardware is needed. On Linux and macOS the tests open a pseudo terminal, which is a real terminal that termios configures exactly as it configures a serial port, so the whole implementation is exercised. On Windows the code is compiled and its error paths are run, but no port is opened, because a virtual COM port needs a driver. With a USB serial adapter and a wire between its TX and RX pins the same tests run against real hardware for about ten dollars.
